At Husky TechnologiesTM, our success is based on your success. Our ability to keep our customers in the lead is based on building the strongest team possible.

Husky TechnologiesTM has a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships and a unique culture and values. We are dedicated to offering our customers the highest quality products and services and are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy. We are a leader in developing state-of-the-art technology and it is this technology base that uniquely positions us to serve customers who seek differentiation through solutions that provide speed, flexibility and maximum productivity. This capability is at the core of our mission and competitive strategy.

Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky Technologies TM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

Discover Hotel PUR, Quebec, a Tribute Portfolio Hotel, where bold design, local spirit and modern hospitality come together in the heart of Quebec City’s vibrant Saint-Roch district. The Director of Finance is responsible for providing ethical and consistent leadership in the financial area of the hotel by supplying management with guidance, training and support. The Director of Finance is also responsible for focusing on the profitability of the business, maintaining accurate and timely financial reporting, ensuring acceptable levels of internal controls, ensuring compliance with all federal, state, and local regulations, and safeguarding owners/investors assets.

Financial:

Acts as the “Chief Business Officer” to the general manager and EC Team, and as such is responsible for evaluating the financial impact on business decisions.
Ensure that all levels of management are promptly notified of any financial deviations from established policies and/or control weaknesses in the hotel.
Effectively manage and communicate cash flow related issues, as required to management and ownership. This includes the accurate and timely preparation of cash-flow statements, management of receivables, cash balances, control mechanisms and timely deposits of all funds.
Monitor hotel revenues and expenses and ensure the accurate recording in accordance with Crescent Hotels & Resorts established guidelines. Investigate and critique variances to budget or to prior year and offer practical improvement strategies to management.
Monitor the capital planning process by assisting management with calculation of return on capital improvements, gathering support and monitoring the bid process, and evaluating scope of work and specifications.

Coordinate the completion of all forecasts and budgets as required, with the full and active participation of EC Team and department managers.
Analyze financial data and operations in order to assist and advise management in maintaining the Hotels’ financial objectives.
Ensure that all balance sheet accounts, including bank reconciliations are reconciled on a timely basis.
Establish and continually audit all internal financial controls including purchasing, cash handling, disbursements, credit extension, inventories, hotel assets, master keys, payroll, and employee records.
Embrace a continuous growth environment by actively hiring professional staff and assisting in recruiting, reviewing, recommending and maintaining an inventory of qualified and promotable Associates that can potentially become Directors of Finance, Assistant Directors of Finance, Accounting Managers, and other managers for the organization.
Continually focus on training and development programs for finance associates to cultivate the “brightest” and “best” talent within the industry.
Hire, train, supervise and develop staff, including coaching, counseling and discipline.
Maintain compliance with Crescent Hotels & Resorts standards and regulations to ensure safe and efficient operation of the hotel.
Ensure proper utilization, maintenance and periodic upgrades of all IT systems and equipments.
Direct and/or prepare all financial reports in accordance with Crescent Hotels & Resorts requirements meeting various due dates and deadlines:
Ensure and monitor that the hotel is in compliance with all report deadlines and due dates and react accordingly.
Maximize efforts towards productivity, identify problem areas and assist in finding and implementing their solutions.
Approach all encounters with guests and employees in an attentive, friendly, courteous and service-oriented manner.
Maintain regular attendance in compliance with Crescent Hotels & Resorts standards, as required by scheduling which will vary according to the needs of the hotel.
Maintain high standards of personal appearance and grooming, which include wearing the professional attire and nametag when working.
Comply at all times with Crescent Hotels & Resorts standards and regulations to encourage safe and efficient hotel operations.

Education & Experience

A minimum of 8 years of related progressive experience in hotel Accounting or related field; or a 4-year college degree with an Accounting/Finance concentration and a minimum of 4 years of related progressive experience; or a 2-year college degree and a minimum of 6 years of related progressive experience.

jobs.description:

An exceptional benefit plan for eligible associates & your family members
RRSP matching program (for eligible associates)

Discounts with Marriott properties globally for you & your family members

Position Summary

The Director of Food & Beverage leads the dining and beverage experience across RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel, from mountain dining and après-ski to upscale restaurant service, weddings and special events.

This hands-on leadership role brings people, service and operations together to create memorable guest experiences, grow the business and build strong teams. The Director will help shape the future of both properties by strengthening standards, developing talent and finding opportunities to work smarter together while preserving each property's unique character.

Major Responsibilities

Top Priorities

Stabilize daily F&B operations and establish clear management routines across both RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel.
Deliver consistent service, culinary quality, atmosphere and cleanliness across every outlet and event, while respecting the different service expectations of mountain dining and an upscale boutique hotel.
Build an accountable F&B leadership team and a reliable seasonal workforce.
Improve revenue, average cheque, labour productivity, cost of sales and departmental profitability.
Strengthen collaboration among Culinary, Service, Banquets, Sales, Events, Rooms and Finance.
Develop beverage, menu, event and après-ski programs.
Create a positive team culture focused on standards, communication, safety and development.
Build relationships with Rossland producers, suppliers, partners and the local community.
Identify shared purchasing, staffing, training, supplier and operational efficiencies across both businesses.
Develop a cohesive F&B strategy that strengthens the overall RED destination experience while maintaining the distinct positioning of each outlet.

Food and Beverage Leadership

Lead the F&B business plan, budget, forecast, service strategy and operating priorities for both businesses, with separate financial accountability and reporting for each.
Maintain visible leadership during peak periods, special events, après-ski and service recovery.
Lead daily and weekly meetings covering forecasts, staffing, reservations, events, product and guest feedback.
Set clear accountability for restaurant, lounge, banquet, culinary, stewarding and beverage leaders.
Provide timely operating updates, risks, results and recommendations to the respective General Managers and senior leadership.
Establish a clear management structure and delegation of responsibilities to ensure both businesses receive consistent leadership and operational oversight.
Work closely with both General Managers to align priorities, resources, budgets and guest experience standards.

Guest Experience And Outlet Operations

Set and inspect standards for greeting, seating, service sequence, menu knowledge, timing, billing and farewell.
Review reservations, covers, groups, events, occupancy, weather and mountain activity to plan each service.
Resolve significant guest concerns, authorize appropriate recovery and correct recurring causes.
Maintain strong outlet presentation, music, lighting, uniforms, cleanliness, equipment and opening and closing controls.
Partner with Rooms and Guest Services on VIPs, amenities, packages, special occasions and in-house communication.
Review guest feedback and online sentiment and turn findings into clear coaching and improvement actions.
Ensure The Josie's F&B operations meet applicable Marriott Autograph Collection brand standards and guest expectations.
Develop distinct service standards appropriate to each outlet, from casual mountain dining to elevated restaurant and hotel experiences.

Culinary and Beverage Partnership

Partner with culinary leaders on menu development, quality, consistency, food cost, production and kitchen execution.
Ensure menus balance guest appeal, local identity, seasonality, operational capacity and financial return.
Lead beverage strategy, pricing, purchasing, inventory, controls, supplier relationships and team education.
Review menu mix, contribution, waste, yields, portioning and availability; act quickly on performance gaps.
Coordinate menu and beverage changes with training, point-of-sale updates, marketing, signage and launch plans.
Identify opportunities to leverage combined purchasing volumes, supplier agreements and beverage partnerships across RED and The Josie.
Oversee the development of distinctive wine, cocktail and beverage programs appropriate to each property's positioning.
Evaluate opportunities for shared culinary resources, menu development and operational efficiencies without compromising quality or service.

Banquets Events and Commercial Performance

Lead F&B execution for meetings, weddings, groups, seasonal activations and hotel events.
Partner with Sales and Events on menus, pricing, service standards, labour, space use and event profitability.
Review banquet event orders and ensure complete handoffs among Sales, Culinary, Service, Rooms and Engineering.
Develop packages, promotions, signature events and local partnerships that grow demand and strengthen positioning.
Track outlet and event revenue, covers, average cheque, pace, mix and conversion against forecast.
Develop a coordinated wedding, conference, group and special events strategy across the resort and hotel, maximizing revenue opportunities for both businesses.
Work with Sales, Marketing and Revenue Management to develop dining experiences, packages and activations that drive incremental visitation, guest spending and destination appeal.
Identify opportunities to improve banquet profitability, event execution and cross-selling between RED and The Josie.

Rebuild People & Culture

Assess structure, talent, procedures and recurring failures; maintain a sequenced improvement plan with both General Managers.
Recruit, onboard, schedule, coach and retain F&B leaders and seasonal employees.
Re-establish pre-shifts, training plans, menu testing, quality checks, labour reviews and manager handovers.
Set clear goals, provide direct feedback, recognize strong performance and address performance concerns promptly.
Build product knowledge, sales confidence, responsible service, food safety and leadership capability.
Create a respectful, inclusive workplace with strong communication and sustainable management coverage.
Build leadership depth at each property, ensuring capable managers are empowered to run day-to-day operations independently.
Develop shared training standards, leadership development opportunities and seasonal staffing strategies where appropriate.
Work with Human Resources to improve recruitment, retention, employee engagement and succession planning across both operations.

Financial Controls Safety and Asset Care

Manage revenue and expenses to budget and forecast, with close attention to labour, food cost, beverage cost and waste.
Review daily sales, discounts, voids, promotions, gratuities, cash, payment activity and operating variances.
Maintain purchasing, receiving, storage, inventory, recipe, portion and point-of-sale controls.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, month-end reporting, capital planning and corrective action for assigned areas.
Ensure compliance with food safety, liquor service, employment, accessibility, privacy, fire and occupational safety requirements.
Protect outlets, kitchens, equipment, smallwares and inventories through disciplined maintenance and asset stewardship.
Maintain separate departmental budgets, financial reporting and performance measures for RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel.
Work with Finance to establish transparent and appropriate allocation of shared costs, labour and purchasing between the two businesses.
Identify opportunities for consolidated procurement, improved supplier pricing and operational efficiencies.
Partner with Engineering and Finance to prioritize deferred maintenance, equipment replacement and capital improvements across F&B operations.

Measures of Success

Guest satisfaction, online sentiment, complaint recurrence, recovery time, service timing and quality consistency.
Outlet and banquet revenue, covers, average cheque, menu mix, upselling and event conversion.
Labour productivity, overtime, food cost, beverage cost, waste, inventory accuracy and departmental profitability.
Health inspection, food safety, responsible service, cash control, inventory and workplace safety performance.
Leadership stability, seasonal staffing readiness, retention, attendance, training completion and internal development.
Completion of agreed rebuild milestones and reduction in repeat service, product and control failures.
Improvement in F&B profitability at both RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel, measured independently.
Demonstrable purchasing savings and operating efficiencies achieved through appropriate shared services.
Growth in banquet, wedding, group and special event revenue across both properties.
Successful development of a stable management structure capable of supporting two distinct F&B operations.

Key Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Education

Post-secondary education in business administration, hospitality, tourism, culinary arts, or a related field is preferred; equivalent relevant experience will be considered.
Additional hospitality, food safety, or responsible beverage service education or certification is an asset.

Experience

Seven or more years of progressive F&B leadership experience, preferably including senior management responsibility within a full-service hotel, resort or multi-outlet hospitality operation.
Experience leading multiple outlets and supervising managers or supervisors across culinary, service, bar and event operations.
Demonstrated experience with budgets, forecasting, labour management, inventory control, menu costing and pricing, and improving financial performance.
Experience with point-of-sale systems and scheduling, inventory, reservation, event and other business software.
Experience overseeing both hotel F&B operations and high-volume casual dining or resort outlets is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated success improving underperforming operations, developing management teams and implementing sustainable operating standards.
Experience with banquets, weddings, conferences and group business is strongly preferred.
Experience with Marriott or another internationally branded hotel is an asset.

Physical And Other Requirements

Ability to meet the physical demands of an active resort and hotel environment, with reasonable accommodation where required.

jobs.title: Head of Supply Chain - Canada
jobs.description:
Your Tasks

Supply chain strategy and operations

Define and deliver the Canadian supply chain strategy, annual operating plan and improvement roadmap, aligned with country and North America priorities. Oversee product availability, order fulfilment, warehousing, transportation and finished goods inventory, balancing service, cost, working capital and risk. Ensure capacity and contingency plans support promotions, seasonal peaks, growth and continuity. Lead recovery from supply and logistics disruptions.

Demand planning and S&OP

Lead and develop the Demand Planning team, setting objectives for forecast accuracy, bias and planning quality, and addressing performance gaps. Provide direction, resources and constructive challenge while the team owns demand plan development. Ensure sound assumptions aligned with Sales, Marketing and Finance. Own Supply Chain's S&OP contribution, presenting demand and supply risks, capacity constraints, inventory and cost implications. Secure country and North America decisions and deliver agreed actions.

Customer replenishment and collaboration

Lead and develop the Customer Replenishment and Collaboration team, setting strategy and goals for service, on-shelf availability, inventory and customer supply chain relationships. Provide direction, coaching and resources, aligning replenishment and collaboration priorities with Sales and Canadian objectives. Be accountable for team performance and relationship outcomes. Support strategic customer discussions and escalations, and ensure improvement plans address service gaps and avoidable costs.

Value Added Services (VAS) and rework

Define VAS strategy, priorities and targets; own service, cost and quality performance. Direct and support the VAS Manager on capacity, providers and delivery. Support manager-led continuous improvement, cost efficiency and waste reduction, securing resources for capability and capacity needs. Ensure traceability and inventory controls, with Quality and Regulatory alignment on specifications, approvals and release.

Innovation and product changes

Be accountable for the North America Project Management team's performance in delivering Canadian innovations and product changes on time, within budget and to customer requirements. Ensure Canadian business and customer needs are captured early in scope, milestones, dependencies and timelines, supporting customer setup, launch readiness and delivery dates. Agree Canadian priorities, responsibilities and commitments with regional project leaders. Review progress, secure corrective actions and resources, and escalate delivery risks.

North America service delivery and governance

Represent Canadian requirements in regional planning, logistics and shared-service decisions, ensuring North America priorities support local commitments. Agree service levels, responsibilities, performance measures and escalation routes with regional functions serving Canada. Review service quality, reliability, responsiveness and cost. Secure resources and corrective actions with owners and timelines; ensure sustained results. Influence across reporting lines and resolve competing priorities while retaining accountability for Canadian operations.

Budget and cost delivery

Own the Canadian supply chain budget, rolling forecasts and approved cost targets, including North America service costs. Manage warehousing, transportation, VAS, rework, inventory write-offs, customer penalties and other supply chain costs. Partner with Finance to explain variances, validate charges and accruals, and implement corrective actions. Assess cost to serve by customer, channel and activity. Deliver measurable savings and productivity improvements while maintaining service and quality. Build investment, outsourcing and network change business cases.

Your Profile

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Operations Management or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Typically +10-15 or more years of progressive supply chain experience, including at least 5 years leading teams and substantial operational scope; consumer packaged goods or a comparable retail-driven environment preferred.
Preferred experience using OMP, SAP, Oracle or similar tools for Supply Planning
Demonstrated experience in demand planning, customer replenishment, logistics, inventory management, VAS or co-packing, and product launch or change implementation.
Proven ownership of supply chain budgets, cost improvement, logistics tenders and third-party provider performance in the Canadian market.
Strong matrix leadership, negotiation and change management skills, with the ability to influence regional stakeholders and communicate clear, fact-based recommendations.
Proficiency with enterprise resource planning, advanced planning and business intelligence tools. SCMP, ASCM CPIM or CSCP, or PMP certification is an asset.
Professional proficiency in French and English to work with Canadian / Quebec stakeholders and collaborate regularly with English and Spanish -speaking customers and service providers.

Power Factors lutte contre les changements climatiques avec le code.

À l'extérieur de la Chine et de l'Inde.

About Blue J

Blue J is the leading generative AI solution for tax professionals and one of Canada's fastest-growing AI companies. Headquartered in Toronto, we're a high-growth B2B SaaS company building industry-leading tax research software that helps accountants find accurate answers to complex tax questions with greater speed and confidence, supporting workflows across compliance, advisory, training, tax writing, and more.

Backed by a $176M USD Series E funding round, we're scaling rapidly across North America and the UK while continuing to push the boundaries of what's possible with AI. By combining advanced technology with deep tax expertise, we empower tax professionals to work more efficiently, make better decisions, and deliver greater value to their clients.

A Note on Location

Primarily remote, but you must live within driving distance of our Toronto office. You’ll join us in person for every quarterly and occasionally for team get-togethers (typically 1–3 visits per quarter).

To help you get off to a great start, we bring all new team members together for their first three days of onboarding. If you’re based outside of our local commuting area, Blue J will arrange and cover your travel and accommodation.

About The Team

Blue J’s technology creates value when tax professionals can easily discover, trust, and incorporate it into their work. The Tax Pro Engagement pillar owns that experience, including onboarding, search, collaboration, account management, purchasing, integrations, and core customer workflows.

As Director of Engineering, you will set the pillar’s technical and organizational direction, lead multiple product-engineering teams, and partner with Engineering and Product leadership to shape priorities and measure customer value.

You will initially immerse yourself in our product, architecture, customers, and codebase while contributing to technical design and complex problem-solving. Over time, your focus will shift toward scaling the teams, leaders, systems, and practices supporting the pillar.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Director of Engineering that will guide the evolution of Blue J’s platform architecture and help our engineering teams deliver high quality products at speed. This role is ideal for someone who is a strong system designer, deeply experienced with building SaaS platforms, and energized by helping teams navigate technical complexity.

The ideal leader combines deep systems expertise with strong product instincts and a genuine commitment to user experience. They will champion the end user, challenge assumptions, and help identify new product possibilities that may not yet be obvious.

You will work closely with product, engineering, and research to define product direction, build reliable and scalable systems, and ensure our teams have the tools and infrastructure they need to ship confidently and frequently. This leader will coach senior engineers, help untangle difficult architectural challenges, jump into code and designs when needed, and grow a team made up of strong software engineers.

This role is designed for a technical leader who enjoys building, mentoring, and shaping the foundational platform that enables world class product development.

What You’ll Be Doing

Setting Direction

Using customer insight, product metrics, and experimentation to guide priorities, evaluate product decisions, and continuously improve the user experience
Collaborating with product and engineering leaders to define goals and priorities
Tying engineering work to measurable outcomes such as activation, adoption, engagement, conversion, retention, workflow completion, performance, and customer trust
Owning the long term vision for platform capabilities that support reliability, scalability, developer experience, and speed of delivery
Identifying focus areas to improve architecture, infrastructure, system performance, and cross team technical alignment

Enabling High Quality Delivery

Leading platform engineers to design and build foundational systems and internal tools
Going deep into architecture and designs to guide teams through ambiguity and complexity
Helping engineers make architectural tradeoffs that balance speed with long term maintainability
Ensuring projects stay on track and are communicated clearly to stakeholders
Supporting teams in shipping frequently, safely, and with high confidence, consistent with Blue J’s engineering culture

Strengthening the Engineering Organization

Coaching and developing engineers into strong system thinkers and leaders
Improving engineering practices that support quality, lean iteration, strong testing, and healthy system design
Hiring high performing engineers and engineering managers who raise the bar
Creating clarity around ownership, mandates, interfaces, and platform boundaries across pods

What You Offer Blue J

10+ years of hands-on experience designing and building heavily used customer facing SaaS products.
5+ years of engineering leadership experience, including responsibility for multiple teams or engineering managers.
Evidence that you have helped shape innovative products and technical direction in partnership with Product and Design, bringing an entrepreneurial and creative mindset rather than simply delivering against an established roadmap.
Strong architectural foundation with experience owning complex systems end-to-end - including roadmap creation, system design, implementation, and long-term evolution.
Ability to design and reason about scalable distributed systems, including performance, reliability, consistency, and cost tradeoffs.
Demonstrated ability to operate as a senior level IC when needed, especially during early context-building.
Track record of identifying critical issues, setting clear goals, and shaping the technical strategy for engineering organizations.
Experience aligning engineering, product, design, and legal research around shared outcomes and coordinated execution.
Clear communication skills with the ability to explain complex system designs to technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience guiding teams through architectural decisions, refactors, and long-term platform modernization.

Additional Experience That Would Be Valuable

Experience with product-led growth, customer activation, experimentation, conversion, engagement, or retention.
Experience building enterprise authentication, authorization, permissions, account structures, collaboration, billing, or purchasing systems.
Experience using product analytics and experimentation to guide technical and product decisions.

Technologies You Can Expect To Work With

These may evolve as our platform grows. Technologies currently in use include:

Node.js, React, TypeScript, Python
AWS, Cloudflare, Terraform
Kubernetes with ArgoCD, Docker
GitHub
PostgreSQL, ElasticSearch, Pinecone, DynamoDB, S3
Kafka, NATS

What We Offer You

A meaningful leadership role shaping the platform foundation of a fast growing company.
A mission-driven culture where your work directly advances clarity, efficiency, and accessibility in tax research.
Competitive base salary, stock options, and benefits designed to support you and your family.
Flexibility in how you work: primarily remote, with occasional travel to our Toronto office
A collaborative, ambitious, and supportive team that values innovation, respect, and fun.
The excitement of a fast-growing, well-funded company with clear momentum, and the resources to back bold initiatives.

The Core Values that Define Our Culture

We are customer-focused
We put team over self
We are pleasant and playful
We are open to better ideas
We move fast and fix things

What To Expect In The Interview Process

We anticipate a high volume of applicants for this role and are excited to grow our team. A human will review each application and get back to you as soon as possible. We appreciate your patience and look forward to connecting with you!

Interview Process

Chat with Elli, our Talent Acquisition Manager
Meet our VP of Engineering, Mario
Technical Deep Dive with an Engineering Team Member
System Design Exercise
Leadership interview with our VP of Engineering, Mario
Meet our CTO, Brett
Meet our CEO, Ben

We believe our strength is built on diversity of thought, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds and experiences to apply. We value inclusiveness and are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

We strive to create an inclusive and accessible hiring experience for all candidates. If you need any accommodations during the interview process, please let us know in your application. Our team is dedicated to providing the necessary support and making reasonable adjustments to ensure a smooth process for everyone.

How We Use AI In Our Hiring Process

To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Blue J uses AI-enabled tools within our applicant tracking system to help organize applications and highlight profiles that match the key requirements for each role.

AI does not make hiring decisions.

Every application is reviewed by a member of our Talent team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans.

We use these tools to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment and we’re committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.

Lead and develop SE leaders and teams, creating accountability for performance while building capability, career growth, and succession within the organization.
Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives that improve technical sales execution, customer experience, and the scalability of the Solutions Engineering function.
Identify technical, operational, and capacity challenges early, develop thoughtful solutions, and proactively resolve dependencies across Sales, Product, Channel, Customer Success, and Implementation.

AEs and channel partners have stronger technical capability and know when and how to engage Solutions Engineering to maximize deal outcomes.
Solution designs can be deployed as sold, improving implementation predictability, customer experience, and margin protection.
The Solutions Engineering organization continuously improves through better processes, feedback loops, technical standards, and an AI-first approach that can scale with the business.

Nice-to-Have:

Experience leading Solutions Engineering teams across multiple customer segments.
Experience with physical security, video surveillance, networking, IoT, AI, or computer vision.
Experience working with channel partners and partner-led technical sales motions.
Experience scaling pre-sales organizations through periods of significant growth.

Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;
Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;
Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

Candidates hired closer to the top of the range will typically demonstrate proficient
capability throughout the interview process. This means they already have the knowledge, skills, and leadership capabilities needed to perform successfully in the role, can ramp up quickly, and are expected to become fully proficient in the position within a short period of time.

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.
